# Carry a kit into Roblox

Use the selected version in `assets/presets.json`; its `native` object maps the visual tokens to Roblox fonts and component properties. Keep the world and gameplay implementation original to the approved specification.

- Build editable `ScreenGui`, frames, layouts and buttons. Use a component factory for each kit's navigation tile, resource strip, item card, detail panel and action button so its geometry, states and spacing remain consistent across screens.
- The supplied SVG paths are authoring assets. Roblox ImageLabels need an imported raster asset with permission for the target experience. Rasterize/upload through the project's approved asset pipeline when available, preserving stable asset mapping. Do not insert a fabricated `rbxassetid`. If that pipeline is unavailable, represent the same distinctive symbols with native UI geometry and record the limitation. Do not silently replace all symbols with empty boxes or text.
- Rasterize glyphs without their sheet labels. Keep English button/item text in separate localizable TextLabels rather than baking it into uploaded pictures.
- Use the pack's native font, contrast, corner radius, stroke and palette. A dark outline around an illustrated icon is separate from a selection border around its card; apply UIStroke to the appropriate container.
- On a phone, give primary actions at least 44 logical pixels and keep currency, navigation and the progress bar away from system and Roblox controls. Simulator navigation becomes a bottom strip; Tactical uses compact grouped equipment; Clicker collapses secondary promotions and navigation. Do not fit by applying a single global UIScale.
- Author labels and placeholders in English. In this workshop, static GUI uses AutoLocalize and the injected `AutomationI18n` source catalogue. Format changing counters and states with keyed complete messages. Leave space for longer translations.
- During game acceptance, measure actual client bounds, text bounds and safe areas on the affected screens. Confirm all item illustrations load and buttons have visible hover/pressed/disabled/selected states. Native tests, source-language checks and published cloud translation retain separate evidence.

The three style previews and icon sheets are reusable visual specifications. Selecting one does not require a Studio scene, a game prototype, a paid image generator or an automatic public upload.

# Visual grammar and source examples

These are independent presentation kits. The three photographs supplied by the user on 2 November 2026 are references for visual decisions, not game screenshots produced by this system. The actual kit assets are original vector illustrations.

## Bright Simulator — `bright-simulator`

Reference: [bright-simulator.png](images/bright-simulator.png).

Use a sunny, spacious playfield, clear colored landmarks and chunky silhouettes. Keep the main objective high and centered; place large illustrated navigation buttons on the left and resource counters near the lower left. White heavy labels with dark outlines and colored raised tiles should read against a bright world. Notifications attach to the relevant button. Shop cards focus on one large item picture with a direct action beneath it; the collection has an obvious selected state.

The world remains visible around the HUD. A restrained screen avoids the right-hand promotional rail and dense progression strip of Neon Clicker. Use studs as an optional material cue, not the only distinction between kits.

## Tactical Tycoon — `tactical-tycoon`

Reference: [tactical-tycoon.png](images/tactical-tycoon.png).

Use industrial silhouettes, a low horizon, metal details and contained cyan signals. Dark beveled panels, compact resource strips, explicit key hints and a bottom equipment belt frame the world. Navigation is a compact horizontal toolbar; menus and shops use side categories and an item list with a separate detail pane. Item illustrations remain essential even though the overall interface is quieter.

Use restrained amber for primary actions, cyan for placement/selection and red for cancellation. The kit should still be identifiable in grayscale by its horizontal information strips, list/detail arrangement and equipment slots.

## Neon Clicker — `neon-clicker`

Reference: [neon-clicker.png](images/neon-clicker.png).

Use a broad plaza, stepped display stands, strong portal silhouettes and luminous accents. The HUD has a two-column illustrated navigation rail, a compact right-hand event/boost rail, and a large bottom progress bar with action tiles. White outlined, slightly slanted labels and saturated gradients give strong hierarchy. Rebirth, gift, gear, world and potion use different symbols, not differently colored copies of one diamond.

Shop products are large illustrated promotion cards; inventory becomes a collection grid. A strong cyan/magenta energy treatment distinguishes this kit from the sunny Simulator. Preserve readable central play space on a phone by collapsing secondary tiles into a menu.

## Compare usefully

The differences concern navigation topology, world composition, information density, typography, item presentation and interaction hierarchy. Check the HUD, menu, shop and inventory rather than accepting a different palette as sufficient. Phone layouts rearrange groups and controls instead of shrinking the whole desktop interface.

# Roblox UI Styles

Use ready-made style kits to make visual choices before building a game. The kits describe presentation and reusable UI components; they do not provide gameplay or a genre template.

## Choose a kit

- Offer the bundled **Bright Simulator**, **Tactical Tycoon** and **Neon Clicker** kits as selectable alternatives. Use [assets/presets.json](assets/presets.json) as the source of versioned tokens and layouts.
- Show the actual kit previews, illustrated icon set and each affected screen. Keep the same sample resources, items and actions when comparing kits. Label these as preset examples, never as screenshots or tests of the user's game.
- Choosing a visual direction does not require building a prototype or connecting Studio. Save the selected kit ID, version and fingerprint in the project; the owner approves the choice before the detailed specification.
- For the visual differences and the user's source photographs, read [references/style-kits.md](references/style-kits.md). Read only the relevant kit when the choice is known.
- If the user asks for a custom variant, preserve its recognizable visual grammar. A palette change alone is not a new style: change the navigation, grouping, action hierarchy, icon treatment and world composition deliberately.
- Preserve an already approved custom or legacy style unless the owner chooses to replace it. Adding this skill to an existing project is not permission to redesign its game.

## Implement the selected kit

Read [references/roblox-implementation.md](references/roblox-implementation.md) when creating or reviewing Roblox UI. Use the selected definition and illustrated symbols in [assets/icons.json](assets/icons.json), together with its preview SVG and icon sheet.

Carry the selected kit through HUD, menu, shop, inventory and world-space UI where those screens are in scope. Keep navigation and currency symbols consistent; give primary actions, secondary actions, disabled states and alerts distinct treatments. Use original bundled shapes rather than emoji, missing external asset IDs or text-only substitutes for promised illustrations.

Game-facing text starts in English (`en-us`) with Roblox localization. Dynamic messages use stable keyed templates and named parameters. Keep player input and names literal. Source-language English and translation readiness are separate from a verified cloud translation.

Preview adaptation is not runtime evidence. Test the produced game in Studio during implementation and acceptance, including actual touch targets, safe areas, text expansion and icon readability. A previously approved preset must not mark those checks passed.

## Bundled resources

- `assets/presets.json`: palette, typography, silhouettes, layout and native implementation tokens.
- `assets/icons.json`: original SVG vector paths for reusable symbols.
- `assets/<kit>-<screen>-<device>.svg`: HUD, menu, shop and inventory examples on desktop and phone.
- `assets/cover-*.svg`: illustrated kit thumbnails.
- `assets/icons-*.svg`: illustrated component sheets for each kit.
- `references/images/*.png`: user-supplied photographs, for visual reference only. Do not carry their player names, brands, event copy or example prices into a new game.

The local workshop automatically pins this skill for art, interface, asset and QA tasks. It is a style layer alongside the project's primary Roblox UI engineering skill, not a second competing engineering standard.
